name: Asian hornet
why: Invasive alien species (SDG 15.8). It hunts honeybees and wild pollinators in front of their nests and weakens bee colonies.
advice: Report it on waarneming.nl with the photo and location. Keep a few metres away from any nest and never try to destroy it yourself: the municipality (gemeente) has nests removed.

name: European hornet
why: Native species. It eats other insects and is usually calm if you leave it alone.
advice: Leave it alone. Recognise it by its yellow-brown thorax and mostly yellow abdomen; the Asian hornet is much darker, with one orange band.

name: Wasp
why: Native species. An important scavenger and pollinator.
advice: Leave it alone. Smaller than a hornet, with a bright yellow-and-black pattern.

name: Hornet hoverfly
why: Native fly that looks like a hornet but cannot sting. A pollinator.
advice: Leave it alone, it is harmless. Recognise it by its big eyes, short antennae and only two wings.

name: Honeybee
why: Pollinator, and the main victim of the Asian hornet.
advice: Leave it alone. Beekeeper? Watch for hornets hovering in front of the hive to hunt.
